evals.name: narrow-github-issue
evals.prompt: I reproduced an Alicit CLI failure in alicit-ai/alicit. Give me the workflow you’d use to file it.
evals.expected_output: A repository-scoped issue filing plan with sanitized evidence.
expectations: Uses the one-repository GitHub runner through Alicit.
Searches for an existing issue before creating one.
Names the repository in the Justification and checks the resulting issue URL.
Keeps secrets and raw credential-bearing output out of the issue.

evals.name: unknown-provider-authority
evals.prompt: I need to change a vendor resource and I can’t find an Alicit Profile for it. What do I do next?
evals.expected_output: Find configured access and describe the exact authority gap.
expectations: Checks live discovery and any configured exact route first.
Distinguishes published capabilities from authorization and explains the reviewed proposal route when applicable.
Does not invent a Profile or fall back to ambient credentials.

evals.name: auth-failure
evals.prompt: Alicit fails before gh can authenticate. Can you report the failure upstream?
evals.expected_output: A sanitized report and a fallback if authenticated reporting is blocked.
expectations: Uses stored diagnostics and the Request outcome when available.
Uses a sanctioned reporter or a ready-to-file local issue body if access is unavailable.
Does not replay failed authentication or use ambient GitHub credentials.

evals.name: kubernetes-exec-lifecycle
evals.prompt: For an enrolled Mac running one dev Pod, can I approve an exec just once, allow it for a day, or leave the rule on until I revoke it? How would I set up and later remove the rule? This is a planning exercise.
evals.expected_output: Explain the three lifetimes and prepare the signed Settings workflow.
expectations: Distinguishes one-off interactive Approval from a signed Settings override.
States the default for a newly authored rule and explicit expires_at: 0 for no expiry.
Scopes the override to one Host or Host Tag, cluster, namespace and exact pod names.
Activates a new draft without --digest, verifies the snapshot digest, and reserves --digest for a stored revision.
Distinguishes stopping future issuance from revoking an existing Invocation in History.

evals.name: no-wake-kubernetes
evals.prompt: Our enrolled Mac needs to pass an existing diagnostic script via stdin to Pod app-dev in namespace dev, context example-cluster. Assume the signed rule was approved. I want the command and what to do if it needs me, without waking me. Planning only.
evals.expected_output: Give the correct local unattended path and distinguish planning from proof.
expectations: Routes execution to the enrolled local host and uses direct kubectl exec with the exact context, namespace and Pod.
Uses --unattended and preserves live stdin with -i and input redirection.
Treats exit 75 as end-of-pass with no Wake and avoids an interactive fallback.
Distinguishes catalog candidates and dry run from authorization and verifies the result against History.

evals.name: mcp-pending
evals.prompt: A GitHub write through the MCP gateway returned pending with a call_id. My foreground tool timed out. What should I check before trying again?
evals.expected_output: Resume the existing call and reconcile uncertain outcomes.
expectations: Uses alicit_result with the original call_id.
Distinguishes the call ID from the retained Request ID and uses the appropriate outcome reader.
Reads back a possibly committed write before considering another Request.

evals.name: git-delivery
evals.prompt: A PR is green, but our repo is mid-migration to Approved Merges. Walk me through deciding which merge route is live and proving the change landed.
evals.expected_output: Select the live approved merge path and verify its effect.
expectations: Checks live activation and chooses the supported merge path.
Binds the operation to the reviewed PR head and avoids broad fallback on refusal.
Verifies the resulting commit with a fresh read.

evals.name: testflight-assignment
evals.prompt: The uploader reported success, but the workflow failed before the TestFlight group assignment. How do we finish this exact build?
evals.expected_output: Verify and assign the existing processed build.
expectations: Inspects App Store Connect for the exact build before retrying.
Uses assignment-only recovery when the upload already happened.
Confirms the processed build is visible to Internal testers.

evals.name: release-skill-parity
evals.prompt: A release was tagged and the cask updated, but the local agent still gives old Alicit advice. How do we prove the binary and skill are current?
evals.expected_output: Check installed CLI and skill separately from publication.
expectations: Checks the actual executable and CLI/Vault versions.
Checks the release-tagged marketplace skill and local installed skill.
Uses the supported CLI qualification/promotion flow and reports any remaining gap.

evals.name: kubernetes-discovery-ambiguity
evals.prompt: Dry run passed, then live kubectl said vaultdynamicsecret matches two API groups. What does the agent do now?
evals.expected_output: Replan the intended fully qualified resource using live evidence.
expectations: Explains that dry run does not query live resource discovery.
Identifies the intended API group before planning the qualified resource name.
Avoids broadening authority or retrying the ambiguous invocation.
